processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Binary Fe-Al alloys with Al contents 4-18 at.% (incl. Fe-4%Al) were prepared by vacuum induction melting in Al2O3 crucibles using Fe with 99.99% purity (purified by zone melting to minimise impurity content) and Al with 99.999% purity.
solidification in Cu moulds to obtain rods usually with 18 mm diameter (as-cast state, used without subsequent heat treatment).

processing_steps.method: electrostatic discharge machining, mechanical polishing, ultrasound cleansing
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Specimens were cut by electrostatic discharge machining, mechanically polished and cleansed by ultrasound in acetone; as-cast material was tested without any subsequent heat treatment.

structures.overall_structure: Polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloy with a coarse grain structure (grain sizes of the order of 1 mm); the as-cast alloys contained no second phases (single-phase Fe-Al solid solution with 4.1 at.% Al).

unmapped_findings: The most ductile Fe-4%Al shows a yield stress drop at -100 °C, which was also observed for Fe-6%Al.
Yield stress drops at -100 °C were produced only by Fe-4%Al (Fig. 4(b)) and Fe-6%Al; no such drops were reported for the other studied alloys.
Fe-4%Al is the most ductile of the polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys of Table 1, showing the largest fracture strain at both room temperature and -100 °C.
Real composition of the Fe-4%Al alloy: 4.1 at.% (2.0 wt.-%) Al; impurities C 60 wt.ppm, Si 100 wt.ppm, and Ni <40 wt.ppm (Table 1).
The yield stress in tension equals that in compression at the same strain rate and temperature for the polycrystalline as-cast alloys, including Fe-4%Al.
At -100 °C the yield stress and ultimate tensile strength of the studied alloys are about 80 MPa higher than at room temperature.
The yield-stress increase with Al content is linear (solid-solution hardening, Suzuki theory) with a hardening coefficient of about 2.2 GPa for the polycrystalline as-cast alloys over 0-18 at.% Al.
